subject: Dedicated cluster configuration options & flexible activation for SkyBridge
messages:

Subject: Dedicated cluster configuration options & flexible activation for SkyBridge

Hi Marta —

Thanks again for the time last week. Attached is a compact proposal that outlines a couple of reserved-capacity options tailored to SkyBridge's forecasted Q3 inference profile. High level: we recommend a two-track structure so you have a cost-predictable baseline while preserving the ability to scale for spikes as your NLU footprint grows.

Option A — "Baseline Lane" (Conservative)
- Minimum committed: 16 A100-equivalent GPUs (sustained)
- Warm pool: 8 GPUs available for burst (pre-warmed, billed at reduced rate)
- Ramp: staged activation over 8 weeks; 25% capacity added every 2 weeks
- SLA target: 95th percentile response < 220ms for 2k tokens workloads

Option B — "Growth Lane" (Aggressive)
- Minimum committed: 48 A100-equivalent GPUs
- Warm pool: 24 GPUs; configurable pre-warm windows for night/day shifts
- Ramp: 4-week activation with optional 2-week accelerated phase if needed
- Burst: up to +60% ephemeral capacity via spot-backed lanes with fallback to smaller model variants

Common controls & notes
- Autoscaling policy: soft-scaling for burst, hard floor is the committed minimum.
- Quantization & model selection: we’ll recommend 8-bit variants for high-throughput routes to reduce cost per token.
- Pre-warm strategy: KV-cache priming window (we recommend 48–72 hours warmup for steady-state traffic; short warmups available for fast launches).
- Change windows: ability to reduce committed GPUs at quarter boundaries with 45-day notice (special case negotiable in SOW).

Attachments in this thread: SB-2391_dedicated_proposal_v1.pdf (proposal deck), SB-2391_pricing_model.xlsx (detailed cost scenarios). Also included a slim warmup_playbook.pdf that describes cache priming and staging steps.

Next steps: can you confirm which SLA tier you want (Standard vs Priority) and a target start date for the activation runway? If you prefer, we can sketch a mutual action plan and lock a DocuSign envelope for the selected lane.

Thanks — happy to jump on quick call if the team wants to walk through the numbers.

—
Dylan Brooks

Dylan —

Thanks for the clear options, appreciate the two-track approach. A couple of clarifying questions before we present to the execs:  

1) On the "Change windows" clause — is the 45-day notice a hard requirement for reducing the baseline, or can we request a one-time mid-quarter reduction with a smaller termination fee? Our usage model can be bursty depending on product campaigns.

2) For the warm pool billing — do we pay full committed rate for those GPUs or a reduced standby rate? Would that change if they are pre-warmed vs cold standby?

3) On latency targets: our SLAs for some endpoints are tighter (150ms p95). If we commit to 48 GPUs can you guarantee 150ms p95 for single-turn completions around 1–2k tokens, or would that require Priority SLA + dedicated routing?

We should also include procurement — looping in procurement@skybridge.ai once we have a lane selected. Can you share a sample SOW clause for mid-quarter contract changes?

Best,
Marta Gonzalez
Head of ML Platform, SkyBridge AI
M: +34 600 111 222

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated cluster configuration options & flexible activation for SkyBridge

Hi Marta —

Quick answers from an ops/architect perspective:  

1) Change window flexibility: the standard contract requires 45 days to reduce baseline to allow for capacity reallocation and billing reconciliation. We can include a one-time "flex reduction" clause in the SOW (typically a 10% of remaining commit redemption fee) to permit a mid-quarter downshift; requires signoff from finance. If this is important, Dylan will add it as a negotiable line item.

2) Warm pool billing: warm pool GPUs are charged at a reduced standby rate (we show this in the pricing sheet) when they are kept idle but pre-warmed. Once moved into active serving (attached to a host), they convert to the committed rate. There is a hybrid hourly metric for partial warm state (small fraction of committed hourly). We'll annotate the spreadsheet to show examples.

3) Latency guarantees: achieving p95 ~150ms for 1–2k tokens depends on model selection and packing. With 48 committed A100-equivalents plus priority routing and local KV cache priming, Priority SLA is realistic for single-turn completions — but we need to pin exact test prompts and expected concurrency. If rigid 150ms p95 is a hard requirement at scale, we recommend the Growth Lane + Priority SLA + evening/day sharding to avoid cold-start noise.

Technical note: pre-warm/priming approach we recommend:
- Stage 1: Load model binaries to hosts and pre-initialize kernels (24–48h)
- Stage 2: KV-cache seeding using representative prompts (48–72h)
- Stage 3: Canary traffic at 5–10% for 12–24h before full cutover

I'll attach a short playbook and a sample SLO table. Happy to run a latency workshop with your infra team next week.

—
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
